items.title: Task 1: Comparing Data From Two Charts Together
items.description: Learn how to identify common themes across two different charts (bar and pie) and write a cohesive overview paragraph.

items.title: Task 1: Describing Processes With Passive Voice
items.description: Master the unique grammar demands of process diagrams using appropriate passive voice and sequencing language (initially, subsequently, finally).

items.title: Task 2: Problem-Solution Essays
items.description: Structure essays that identify problems, propose multiple solutions, and evaluate their feasibility with clear paragraphing.

items.title: Task 2: Exploring Causes and Effects
items.description: Develop essays that explain why something happens (causes) and what results follow (effects) with adequate detail and examples.

items.title: Task 2: 'To What Extent' Opinion Questions
items.description: Respond to questions asking for partial agreement by presenting a clear stance and balancing counterarguments effectively.

items.title: Task 2: Balanced Advantages and Disadvantages Essays
items.description: Present equal weight to both sides of an argument before concluding, avoiding the most common pitfall of unbalanced discussion.

items.title: Paragraph Cohesion: Linking Devices and Transitions
items.description: Use sophisticated linking words (moreover, nevertheless, consequently) and reference chains to create smooth, flowing paragraphs.

items.title: Supporting Main Points With Specific, Relevant Examples
items.description: Learn the difference between vague statements and compelling examples; structure body paragraphs for maximum impact.

items.title: Maintaining Formal Register: Common Lapses and Fixes
items.description: Identify informal language in your drafts (things, lots of, get, really) and replace with academic alternatives (factors, numerous, obtain, significantly).

items.title: Time Management: Planning a Quick Outline Under Pressure
items.description: Develop a 2-minute planning strategy to organize your ideas before writing, reducing the need for extensive revision.

items.title: Addressing the Task Directly and Avoiding Irrelevant Content
items.description: Ensure every paragraph directly responds to the question asked, avoiding tangential discussion that reduces band scores.

items.title: Using Data, Statistics, and Evidence Persuasively
items.description: Incorporate numbers, research, and real-world examples to strengthen arguments and demonstrate critical thinking in task 2.

items.title: Proofreading Checklist: Final 2-Minute Check
items.description: Create a personal checklist of your common errors (spell-check, subject-verb agreement, article use) for last-minute review before submitting.
